Source. `_dwarf_extract_debuglink()` treats the staged `.gnu_debuglink` bytes as a C string. The witness section begins with `0x00`, so this helper accepts the empty name because it only checks that some NUL terminator exists before `endptr`.
The accepted debuglink name is measured as length 0. That emptiness is the value later preserved through path construction.

Even with `namelen == 0`, the debuglink record is not rejected. For this witness the section length is 8 bytes, so the derived CRC pointer lands at byte 4 and the `(crcptr + 4) == endptr` check passes.
The accepted empty string is exported as `debuglink_path_returned`. `dwarf_gnu_debuglink()` later passes this exact non-null empty pointer as `link_string_in` into `_dwarf_construct_linkedto_path()`.
The path-building branch is taken because step 4 produced a non-null pointer, even though the pointed-to string is empty. There is no emptiness check here.

`construct_js()` initialized `joind.js_linkstring` with `dwarfstring_constructor()` so its storage starts as the global literal `""` (`dwarf_string.c:69-74`). Appending step 4's empty string computes zero length and `dwarfstring_append_length()` returns immediately on `slen == 0` (`dwarf_string.c:167-175`), so `joind.js_linkstring` still points to that same global `""`.
`prepare_linked_name()` first copies the executable directory into `out`. This makes the destination path non-empty before `_dwarf_pathjoinl(out, linkname)` is called on step 6's empty link string.

Because step 7 already made `target` non-empty, `_dwarf_pathjoinl()` does not take its `!targlen` early return. It reaches the `is_full_path(inputs, joinchar)` call with `inputs = dwarfstring_string(input)` still pointing to step 6's global `""`.

Root cause and sink. `is_full_path()` never checks whether `path[0]` is NUL before reading `path[1]`. With step 8 calling it on the global empty-string literal still backing `joind.js_linkstring`, this statement reads one byte past the 1-byte `""` object and ASan reports the saved global-buffer-overflow READ.
